intended_object: The altitude of an n-simplex through vertex i: the line through vertex i perpendicular to the opposite face, lying in the affine span of the simplex. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The body intersects two subspaces: the affine subspace through vertex i whose direction is the orthogonal complement of the opposite face's direction, and the affine span of the simplex. Within the n-dimensional span of the simplex, the opposite face's direction has dimension n−1, so its orthogonal complement there is 1-dimensional. The result is exactly the line through the vertex perpendicular to the opposite face. Intersecting with the span keeps this true in higher-dimensional ambient spaces. When n=0 the result is the single point {p₀}, an acceptable convention for a degenerate case. A real inner product space is needed for orthogonality, and the definition works for simplices of any dimension in any Euclidean affine space, so the generality is natural.
